name: Report and investigate incidents
summary: When someone is hurt, nearly hurt, a vehicle is damaged or a line fails on a fracturing, cementing or coiled tubing job, the field supervisor makes the site safe, gives first aid and reports it; a field HSE advisor classifies it, tells the customer, and starts either a short review or a full investigation with witness statements and a root-cause session. The HSE director approves the report, corrective actions are assigned and followed up, and the law sets deadlines: serious incidents phoned to Alberta OHS at once, injury reports to the Workers' Compensation Board within 72 hours, BC investigations within 30 days. Investigations stall because the crew rotates off before statements are taken, approvals wait in the director's queue, and corrective actions sit open for weeks.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company with about 880 field staff on customer leases in Alberta and northeast BC and a small HSE group of field advisors, a director and coordinators.
baseline.notes: Initial reports by phone and paper forms, entered into an HSE incident system; investigations written in Word templates; most work is in Alberta, some in northeast BC.

unit_of_work: one incident or near miss (or one audit finding handled as a case)
trigger: A worker reports an injury, near miss, vehicle or equipment damage incident or spill to the field supervisor, or an audit raises a finding.
end_state: The case is classified, reported to the customer and any regulator or board as required, investigated to the level its severity needs, its corrective actions verified and the case closed; spills are handed to spill response.

volume.seasonality: Follows field activity and new-hire numbers: highest in the winter peak and during the 2021-2022 rehiring; lowest in spring break-up and 2020.

evidence.note: Organisation file volume kept. About 2.5-3 million hours worked a year at a recordable rate near 1 per 200,000 hours gives about one recordable injury a month; near misses, first aid cases, vehicle and property damage make up the rest when near-miss reporting is encouraged (Trican reports tracking hazard identification toward Target Zero).

surge.cause: Winter completion peak with new and recalled crews

evidence.note: Incidents track hours worked and crew inexperience; multiplier estimated.

steps.name: Route the case by where it arose
steps.description: Not a work step: the case starts with the supervisor of the fracturing, cementing or coiled tubing crew where it happened, or with the HSE advisor when it comes from an audit or inspection finding.

evidence.note: Shares follow each service line's share of field hours.

steps.name: Respond and report at the fracturing site
steps.description: The fracturing supervisor stops the work, makes the area safe, gives or arranges first aid, keeps the scene as it is for a serious case, takes names of witnesses, and phones the field HSE advisor and the operations manager with what happened.

error.defect_description: Scene disturbed or witnesses leave before names are taken.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act s.33 duty to report and preserve the scene of serious incidents; company incident reporting standard

evidence.note: Serious incidents are phoned to OHS as soon as possible and the scene preserved (OHS Act s.33(2)); times tier C.

steps.name: Respond and report at the cementing site
steps.description: The cementing supervisor stops the work, makes the area safe, gives or arranges first aid, keeps the scene as it is for a serious case, takes names of witnesses, and phones the field HSE advisor and the operations manager with what happened.

error.defect_description: Scene disturbed or witnesses leave before names are taken.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act s.33 duty to report and preserve the scene of serious incidents; company incident reporting standard

evidence.note: Serious incidents are phoned to OHS as soon as possible and the scene preserved (OHS Act s.33(2)); times tier C.

steps.name: Respond and report at the coiled tubing site
steps.description: The coiled tubing supervisor stops the work, makes the area safe, gives or arranges first aid, keeps the scene as it is for a serious case, takes names of witnesses, and phones the field HSE advisor and the operations manager with what happened.

error.defect_description: Scene disturbed or witnesses leave before names are taken.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act s.33 duty to report and preserve the scene of serious incidents; company incident reporting standard

evidence.note: Serious incidents are phoned to OHS as soon as possible and the scene preserved (OHS Act s.33(2)); times tier C.

steps.name: Open a case for an audit finding
steps.description: The HSE advisor opens a case in the HSE system for a serious or repeated audit or inspection finding, such as missing hazard assessments or an uncertified line, so it gets the same classification and corrective action tracking as an incident.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Take the injured worker for treatment
steps.description: The HSE advisor or a designated driver takes the worker to the nearest clinic or hospital, stays with them, explains modified work options to the doctor, and reports the diagnosis back to the operations manager.

evidence.note: Common case-management practice in Canadian field services to manage WCB claims; times estimated.

steps.name: Classify the incident and its potential severity
steps.description: The HSE advisor decides the type (near miss, first aid, medical aid, lost time, vehicle, property damage, spill), rates the actual and potential severity on the company matrix, decides whether it is reportable to OHS, WorkSafeBC or the board, and sets the investigation level.

error.defect_description: Potential severity rated too low, so a full investigation is skipped.

next.condition: spill or release handed to spill response

evidence.note: Employers investigate with worker representatives, write reports with corrective actions and keep them 2 years; BC full investigation within 30 days. Times tier C.

steps.name: Phone the regulator and preserve the scene
steps.description: The HSE director phones the Alberta OHS Contact Centre or WorkSafeBC, confirms with the customer as prime contractor who reports, keeps the scene undisturbed until an officer releases it, and calls the executive team and insurer.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act s.33 serious incident reporting and scene preservation; BC Workers Compensation Act immediate notice

evidence.note: Serious incidents are phoned to OHS as soon as possible and the scene preserved (OHS Act s.33(2)); times tier C.

steps.name: Notify the customer's representative
steps.description: The HSE advisor calls the customer's wellsite supervisor or HSE contact with the facts known so far, as most master service agreements require within hours, and agrees who investigates when the customer is prime contractor on the lease.

control.basis: Customer master service agreement incident notification terms

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Enter the initial report in the HSE system
steps.description: The HSE advisor types the initial report from the supervisor's notes and form: date, site, crew, people involved, description, immediate actions, classification and photos, and emails the flash report to operations management.

error.defect_description: Facts typed from second-hand notes are wrong or incomplete.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Submit the employer report of injury
steps.description: The HSE coordinator completes the employer report of injury in myWCB or the WorkSafeBC employer report with the worker's details, hours and treatment, arranges modified duties with the operations manager, and records the claim number.

error.defect_description: Report filed after 72 hours or with wrong hours.

control.basis: Alberta Workers' Compensation Act: employer report within 72 hours (Form 7 in BC)

evidence.note: Employer report of injury within 72 hours of becoming aware of an injury with lost time, modified work or treatment beyond first aid; times tier C.

steps.name: Review a low-potential case
steps.description: For near misses and first aid cases with low potential, the advisor talks to the supervisor, records the immediate cause and the fix, such as a toolbox talk or a guard replaced, and decides whether any action needs tracking.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Collect statements and evidence
steps.description: The advisor gets written statements from the people involved and witnesses, photos, gas monitor and data van records, maintenance history and the day's hazard assessment; when the crew has rotated off, statements wait for their next shift or are taken by phone.

evidence.note: Employers investigate with worker representatives, write reports with corrective actions and keep them 2 years; BC full investigation within 30 days. Times tier C.

steps.name: Run the root-cause session
steps.description: The advisor leads a causal analysis with the supervisor, a worker representative and the operations manager, building the timeline and finding the immediate and underlying causes such as a missing procedure, training gap or worn equipment.

control.basis: Worker representative or committee participation in investigations (Alberta OHS Act; BC Workers Compensation Act)

evidence.note: Employers investigate with worker representatives, write reports with corrective actions and keep them 2 years; BC full investigation within 30 days. Times tier C.

steps.name: Write the investigation report
steps.description: The advisor writes the report in the company template: description, timeline, causes, and corrective actions with owners and due dates, with photos and statements attached.

error.defect_description: Corrective actions are vague (retrain, be careful) or have no owner.

evidence.note: Employers investigate with worker representatives, write reports with corrective actions and keep them 2 years; BC full investigation within 30 days. Times tier C.

steps.name: HSE director reviews and approves the report
steps.description: The HSE director reads the report, checks the causes support the actions and that the severity rating is right, sends it back for gaps, and signs it off for the customer and, where required, the regulator.

control.basis: Company incident management standard: director approval of investigations

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Submit the investigation to the regulator
steps.description: The HSE coordinator submits the report through the Alberta OHS online service for potentially serious or serious incidents, or the employer incident investigation report to WorkSafeBC within 30 days, and files the confirmation.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act s.33(6) potentially serious incident report; BC Workers Compensation Act 30-day full investigation report

evidence.note: Submission after investigation (Alberta) and within 30 days (BC); share and times tier C.

steps.name: Send the report to the customer
steps.description: The advisor emails the approved report to the customer's HSE contact, often in the customer's own format or portal, and books a call to walk through causes and actions.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Customer reviews the report
steps.description: The customer's HSE group reviews the report against its contractor management standard, asks questions or more actions, and may raise it at the next contractor performance review.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Issue a safety alert
steps.description: The advisor writes a one-page alert with what happened and what to do differently, gets it approved, and sends it to all districts for the next safety meetings.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Log corrective actions and training needs
steps.description: The HSE coordinator enters each corrective action with owner and due date in the HSE system and sends training needs, such as a refresher course for a crew, to the training group.

error.defect_description: Action logged without owner or due date.

control.basis: BC corrective action report with owners and dates; Alberta investigation report with corrective actions

evidence.note: Employers investigate with worker representatives, write reports with corrective actions and keep them 2 years; BC full investigation within 30 days. Times tier C.

steps.name: Verify corrective actions are done
steps.description: When owners report actions done, the advisor checks evidence on site or in records, such as a new procedure issued, equipment repaired or training completed, and closes each action; overdue actions are flagged.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Chase overdue actions
steps.description: The HSE coordinator sends the overdue action list to owners and their managers and raises long-overdue items at the monthly operations meeting.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Close the case and update statistics
steps.description: The HSE coordinator closes the case, checks the classification used for recordable injury and vehicle incident rates, and includes it in the monthly safety statistics for management, customers and prequalification portals.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Serious incident
exceptions.description: A hospital admission, fire or line failure that must be phoned to the regulator, with the scene held until released.

exceptions.name: Witnesses rotated off
exceptions.description: The crew finishes its rotation before statements are taken; the investigation waits a week or more.

exceptions.name: Report sent back
exceptions.description: The director or the customer finds weak causes or vague actions and the report is rewritten.

exceptions.name: Overdue corrective actions
exceptions.description: Owners miss due dates and the coordinator chases them through monthly meetings.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from report to case closed
benchmarks.population: Incidents and near misses at a Canadian oilfield service company, 2019-2022

evidence.note: No published closure time found. Rests on about a third of cases being low-potential near misses closed within days, other short reviews closing when their actions are done in two to three weeks, and full investigations taking about a month plus corrective action follow-up, consistent with the BC 30-day deadline for full investigations (wsbc-inv).

benchmarks.metric: fleet kilometres without a severe vehicle accident

pain_points.description: Crews rotate off before statements are taken, so investigations stall for a week or more.

evidence.note: Organisation file process description; field rotations of 14 days on and 7 off.

pain_points.description: Reports wait for the director's approval and the customer's review, pushing full investigations past a month.

evidence.note: General knowledge; BC requires full investigations within 30 days (wsbc-inv is the benchmark source).

pain_points.description: Corrective actions are vague or have no owner, and many stay open past their due dates.

evidence.note: WorkSafeBC asks for corrective actions with names and completion dates and a check of their effect; the shortfall is tier C.

pain_points.description: Potential severity is rated low to avoid a full investigation or a reportable classification.

evidence.note: General knowledge of incident classification pressures when customers score contractors on safety statistics.

sources.title: Trican Well Service Ltd. Issues 2021 ESG Report (news release)
sources.supports: In 2021 the fleet travelled 25.2 million kilometres with no severe vehicle accidents; over $475,000 spent on employee training.

sources.title: Report serious injuries, illnesses or incidents
sources.supports: Call the OHS Contact Centre as soon as possible for a death, a worker admitted to hospital, an unplanned explosion, fire or flood that could cause serious injury, crane or derrick collapse, or structural failure; do not disturb the scene (OHS Act s.33(2)) except to help the injured or prevent further harm; the prime contractor, or the employer if none, investigates with the joint health and safety committee or representative, prepares a written report on the circumstances and prevention, gives it to OHS, and keeps it for at least 2 years.

sources.title: Report potentially serious incidents
sources.supports: A potentially serious incident (one with a likelihood of causing serious injury or illness) must be investigated by the employer or prime contractor, with a report describing the investigation and corrective actions; the report is submitted online after the investigation is complete (OHS Act s.33(6)), given to the health and safety committee or representative, and kept for at least 2 years.

sources.title: Report an injury - for employers
sources.supports: Employers must submit the employer report of injury within 72 hours of becoming aware of an injury that causes lost time, modified work beyond the day of injury, treatment beyond first aid or medical aid expenses; reported through myWCB online, the employer app, a one-time online form or the faxed C040 form.

sources.title: Conducting an employer investigation
sources.supports: BC employers must investigate serious injuries, injuries needing medical treatment, and incidents with potential for serious injury; preliminary investigation and report within 48 hours; interim corrective actions; full investigation and report within 30 days submitted to WorkSafeBC; corrective action report naming the actions, owners and completion dates; an employer and a worker representative take part; copies to the joint committee or worker representative.

assumptions: Loaded cost per hour comes from the organisation file (base wage x 1.35).
Step s01 is a routing step with no work, so that the first responder of each service line is shown.

Alberta rules changed in the period: the OHS Act of 2017 and its 2020 replacement (in force September 2021) changed how potentially serious incidents are reported; the file follows the current published guidance of reporting after investigation. Serious incident calls, scene preservation and the 72-hour board report applied throughout.
On customer leases the producer is often the prime contractor and leads or co-leads serious investigations; the company still investigates its own incidents.
Spills are classified here and handed to hs-environmental-spill-response, which is not in the process map's links for this process.
Cementing and coiled tubing supervisors respond to incidents on their jobs but are not in the process map's role list.
